outcome: surgical intervention (manual placental removal/aspiration/curettage, intrauterine balloon tamponade, uterine packing, compression sutures)
cohort: The study included 1038 patients who gave birth at the Hannover Medical School between January 2013 and August 2022 and experienced postpartum hemorrhage (blood loss >= 500 ml after vaginal delivery or >= 1000 ml after cesarean section).
finding: The study identified specific risk factors, including nicotine abuse, uterine malformation, C-section, and abnormal placentation, associated with severe blood loss, surgical intervention, and peripartum hysterectomy in patients experiencing postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: C-section was identified as an independent risk factor for severe blood loss and the need for operative management in cases of postpartum hemorrhage.
